[text-1] "For my ultimate Chocolate Chip Cookies, see here (it requires overnight refrigeration and worth the wait!)."
[text-2] "Chocolate Chip Cookie recipe"
[text-3] "A long awaited reader request…. I’ve lost count of the number of times I’ve had people writing in asking for my chocolate chip cookie recipe!"
[text-4] "In truth, I was sitting on it because I wanted to make sure I tested it properly for different measures in different countries. If you’ve ever tried a cookie recipe written by someone in another country and had it fail miserably, chances are that it’s because of the difference in cup, tablespoon and"
[text-5] "For most recipes, the difference between measures is not enough to affect the recipe or the difference is proportional across the whole recipe so it still works fine. However, for baking recipes, you really have to be careful. Especially cookies and cakes."
[text-6] "So that’s a little tip for you when using baking recipes – check the country of origin of the writer. If it’s not your country, proceed with caution! 😉"
[text-7] "Oh – in case I forgot to make it really clear – yes I’ve tested this recipe using Australian & rest of world cups (all exc US are very similar) and US cups and weight measures."
[text-8] "Oh – and this is based on a Cooks’ Illustrated tried and tested recipe. That always helps!"
[text-9] "This chocolate chip cookie recipe may be a little different to most you’ve come across. It’s unique in that there’s no creaming butter, no electric beater is required, there’s no refrigeration of the dough (unless it’s stinking hot where you are!) and there’s no rolling dough."
[text-10] "Dump and mix. The batter will be quite soft at first because of the melted butter, but after 5 minutes or so, it firms up into a soft dough that can be scooped onto the baking tray and it holds its form perfectly. Using an ice cream scooper with a lever (seriously handy kitchen utensil – cookies, pa"
[text-11] "I’ve tried to capture how soft these cookies are in the recipe video (below the recipe). I hope I’ve succeeded. I also hope I’ve succeeded in showing you how straight forward these are to make."
[text-12] "Dangerous. I should have called these Dangerous Choc Chip Cookies."
[text-13] "Happy weekend everyone! – Nagi xx"

[text-20] "Byron Bay copycat cookies – Choc Chunk, White Choc Macadamia and Chewy Choc Fudge"
[text-21] "PS That moment when I smack my mother’s hand in the video….. I have been wanting an excuse to do that all my life…."
[text-22] "PPS This recipe makes big cookies about 10cm/4″ wide. I have a cookie baking session planned this weekend and plan to test out different sizes for bake times and will update the recipe! <– Said baking session took place, recipe updated for directions for small cookies!"
[text-23] "PPPS I don’t know why it is but my recipes always seem to come out with odd numbers. This recipe makes 13 cookies. THIRTEEN. My trays fit 6 each perfectly. Which means I have to have a third tray…..for just ONE cookie. 🙄"
[text-24] "Watch How To Make It"
[text-25] "Soft Chocolate Chip Cookies recipe video!"
[text-26] "HUNGRY FOR MORE? Subscribe to my newsletter and follow along on Facebook, Pinterest and Instagram for all of the latest updates."
[text-27] "Soft Easy Chocolate Chip Cookies"
[text-28] "206"
[text-29] "1920"
[text-30] "RECIPE VIDEO ABOVE. This is my I need chocolate chip cookies now recipe that makes soft, buttery cookies. No waiting for butter to soften, no electric beater, no refrigeration time, no rolling dough into balls. The hardest part is waiting for them to cool!"
[text-31] "Adapted from Cooks Illustrated. Makes 13 large or 26-30 small. {This recipe will work no matter which country you live in – see Note 5. High altitude baking – see Note 6.}"
[text-32] "Note: For my Rolls Royce Chocolate Chip Cookies, see here (it requires overnight refrigeration and worth the wait!)."
[text-33] "Ingredients"
[text-34] "▢ 1 3/4 cups plain / all purpose flour"
[text-35] "▢ 1 tsp salt"
[text-36] "▢ ½ tsp baking soda (bi carb soda)"
[text-37] "▢ 175g / 12 tbsp unsalted butter , cut into 2 cm/ 4/5″ cubes (1.5 US sticks / 6 oz)"
[text-38] "▢ 1/2 cup brown sugar , packed (light or dark) (Note 1)"
[text-39] "▢ 1/2 cup caster sugar (US: granulated sugar)"
[text-40] "▢ 1 egg"
[text-41] "▢ 1 egg yolk"
[text-42] "▢ 2 tsp vanilla extract"
[text-43] "▢ 1 1/4 cups chocolate chips , separated (US: semi sweet chocolate chips or chunks)"
[text-44] "Instructions"
[text-45] "Preheat oven to 180C / 350F (standard) or 160C/320F (fan / convection). Place oven shelf in the middle of the oven."
[text-46] "Line 2 trays with baking / parchment paper."
[text-47] "Whisk the flour, salt and baking soda in a bowl."
[text-48] "Place the butter in a large heatproof bowl. Microwave until the butter is almost fully melted (25 sec for room temp butter, 40 sec for fridge cold butter on high)."
[text-49] "Whisk to finish melting the butter. (Note 2)"
[text-50] "Add brown and white sugar, whisk energetically for 15 seconds."
[text-51] "Add egg, yolk and vanilla, whisk well for 15 seconds."
[text-52] "Add flour mixture and mix until flour is almost fully incorporated."
[text-53] "Add 1 cup chocolate chips, stir to disperse and flour is fully incorporated. Batter will be quite loose."
[text-54] "Stand for 5 minutes for batter to firm up a bit so it is scoop-able into mounds. (Note 3)"
[text-55] "LARGE COOKIES: Scoop up a level ice cream scoop / 3 tbsp / 1/4 cup (Note 4) and place on baking trays 5cm / 2″ apart – 13 balls. Top with remaining choc chips (these remain on surface once baked = prettier)."
[text-56] "SMALL COOKIES (26 – 30): Scoop up 1.5 tbsp (heaped tbsp measure) OR 1/2 an ice cream scoop (this works well). Place on baking trays 4cm / 1.75″ apart, top with choc chops."
